blocks.text: [1, 2] [Arabic, p. 170] [^n3086]And one of his disciples was sitting[^n3087] in his bosom, he whom Jesus loved. [^n3088]To him Simon Cephas beckoned, that he should ask him who this was, concerning [3] whom he spake. [^n3089]And that disciple leaned[^n3090] on Jesus’ breast, and said unto him, [4] My Lord, who is this? [^n3091]Jesus answered and said, He to whom I shall dip bread, and give it. And Jesus dipped bread, and gave to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. [5] [^n3092]And after the bread, Satan entered him. And Jesus said unto him, What thou [6] desirest to do, hasten the doing of it. [^n3093]And no man of them that sat knew why he [7] said this unto him. [^n3094]And some of them thought, because Judas had the box, that he was bidding him buy what would be needed for the feast; or, that he might pay [8] something to the poor. [^n3095]Judas the betrayer answered and said, Can it be I, my [9] Master? Jesus said unto him, Thou hast said. [^n3096]And Judas took the bread straightway, and went forth without: and it was still night.

[10] [^n3097]And Jesus said, Now is the Son of man being glorified,[^n3098] and God is being glorified[^n3099] [11] in him; [^n3100]and if God is glorified in him, God also will glorify him in him, and straightway will glorify him.

[12] [^n3101]And while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and divided; [^n3102]and he [13] gave to his disciples, and said unto them, Take and eat; this is my body. [^n3103]And he [Arabic, p. 171] took a cup, and gave thanks, and blessed, and gave them, [^n3104]and said, Take [14, 15] and drink of it, all of you. [^n3105]And they drank of it, all of them. [^n3106]And he said unto them, [^n3107]This is my blood, the new covenant, that is shed for many for the [16] forgiveness of sins. [^n3108]I say unto you, I shall not drink henceforth of this, the juice of the vine, until the day in which I drink[^n3109] with you new wine in the kingdom of [17] God. [^n3110]And thus do ye in remembrance of me. [^n3111]And Jesus said unto Simon, Simon, [18] behold, Satan asketh that he may sift you like wheat: [^n3112]but I entreat[^n3113] for thee, that thou lose not thy faith:[^n3114] and do thou, at some time, turn[^n3115] and strengthen thy brethren.

[19] [^n3116]My children, another little while am I with you. And ye shall seek me: and as [20] I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; I say unto you now also. [^n3117]A new commandment I give you, that ye may love one another; and as I have loved [21] you, so shall ye also love one another. [^n3118]By this shall every man know that ye are [22] my disciples, if ye have love one to another. [^n3119]Simon Cephas said unto him, Our Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered and said unto him, Whither I go, thou canst not now follow me; but later thou shalt come.

[23] [^n3120]Then said Jesus unto them, Ye all shall desert[^n3121] me this night:[^n3122] it is written, I [24] will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered. [^n3123]But after my [25] rising, I shall go before you into Galilee. [^n3124]Simon Cephas answered and said unto [26] him, My Lord, if every man desert thee, I shall at no time desert thee. [^n3125]I am with thee ready for imprisonment and for death. [^n3126]And my life will I give up for thee. [27] [Arabic, p. 172] [^n3127]Jesus said unto him, Wilt thou give up thy life for me? [^n3128]Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Thou shalt to-day, during this night, before the cock crow [28] twice, three times deny me, that thou knowest me not. [^n3129]But Cephas said the more,[^n3130] Even if it lead to[^n3131] death with thee, I shall not deny thee, my Lord. And in like manner said all the disciples also.

[29] [^n3132]Then Jesus said unto them, Let not your hearts be troubled:[^n3133] believe in God, [30] and believe in me. [^n3134]The stations[^n3135] in my Father’s house are many, else I should [31] have told[^n3136] you. I[^n3137] go to prepare for you a place. [^n3138]And if I go to prepare for you a place, I shall return again, and take you unto me: and so where I am, there ye [32, 33] shall be also. [^n3139]And the place that I go ye know,[^n3140] and the way ye know.[^n3141] [^n3142]Thomas said unto him, Our Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how is the way for [34] us to the knowledge of that?[^n3143] [^n3144]Jesus said unto him, I am the way, and the truth, [35] and the life: and no man cometh unto my Father, but through me. [^n3145]And if ye had known me, ye should have known my Father: and from henceforth ye know[^n3146] him, [36] and have seen him. [^n3147]Philip[^n3148] said unto him, Our Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth [37] us. [^n3149]Jesus said unto him, Have I been all this time with you, and dost thou not know[^n3150] me, Philip?[^n3151] whosoever hath seen me hath seen the Father; how then sayest [38] thou, Shew us the Father? [^n3152]Believest thou not that I am in my Father, and my Father in me? and the saying that I say, I say not of myself: but my Father who dwelleth in [39] me, he doeth these deeds. [^n3153]Believe that I am in my Father, and my Father in me: [40] [Arabic, p. 173] or else believe for the sake of the deeds. [^n3154]Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever believeth in me, the deeds that I do shall he do also; and [41] more than that shall he do: I go unto the Father. [^n3155]And what ye shall ask in my [42] name, I shall do unto you, that the Father may be glorified in his Son. [^n3156]And if ye [43, 44] ask me[^n3157] in my name, I will do it. [^n3158]If ye love me, keep my commandments. [^n3159]And I will entreat of my Father, and he will send unto you another Paraclete, that he [45] may be with you for ever, even the Spirit of truth: [^n3160]whom the world cannot receive; for it hath not seen him, nor known him: but ye know him; for he hath dwelt[^n3161] [46] with you, and is in you. [^n3162]I will not leave you orphans: I will come unto you. [47] [^n3163]Another little while, and the world seeth me not; but ye see me that I live, and ye [48] shall live also. [^n3164]And in that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.

n3098.text: A simple change of diacritical points would give the reading of the Greek and of the Syriac versions.

n3099.text: A simple change of diacritical points would give the reading of the Greek and of the Syriac versions.

n3109.text: Peshitta adds it. The reading of the Sinaitic is doubtful.

n3114.text: We may translate, with the Syriac versions, that thy faith fail not, only if we assign a somewhat Syriac meaning to the verb, and assume either an error in diacritical points (t for y) or an unusual (Syriac) gender for faith.

n3121.text: The Arabic word is not unlike the word for stumble, and Borg. ms. omits me.

n3131.text: Lit. end in. Or, if I come to (the point of).

n3133.text: The diacritical points in both Vat. (followed by Ciasca) and Borg. mss. appear to demand a rendering inquire for be troubled. In Ibn-at-Tayyib’s comments (not the text), however (with other points), we have the meaning wail (root nhb). Every Syriac version uses a different word.

n3137.text: Probably the Arabic represents a Syriac For I.

n3143.text: cf. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary (f. 352a) and order of words in Peshitta (not Sin.).

n3150.text: More exactly, hast thou not come to know.

n3157.text: The Borg. ms. has me clearly (cf. Peshitta). The Vat. ms. is ambiguous.

n3161.text: Probably a misreading of the Peshitta (not Sin. or Cur.), since the next clause also agrees with it.
